searchText: Haven't seen it mentioned anywhere (probably missed it), but the final Blst audit report is out: https://research.nccgroup.com/2021/01/20/public-report-blst-cryptographic-implementation-review/ There is a mistake in the report here > The min-pk configuration’s signing process CoreSign() 19 function may very well be a publicly-observable repeated operation of the above nature, and thus of higher risk. Proof-of-stake users in this configuration emit signatures under a high-value key on a regular basis. Note that Ethereum 2 operates in the min-sig configuration. Eth2 uses min-pk Note that since then BLST changed to Pornin's inversion algorithm 😉 Does anyone know where to find explicit formulas for (2^n)P+Q, where P and Q are in an elliptic curve group, and n is a small positive integer. The closest I can find is in the appendix of Dimitrov, Imbert, Mishra, "The Double-Base Number System and Its Application to Elliptic Curve Cryptography", but the underlying doublings look inefficient -- it is from 2008. Hisil's 2010 thesis future ideas section says "this is a big gap in the literature to be filled." Hopefully it has been filled since 2010. I am considering expanding the expressions on paper and looking for common subexpressions to eliminate, but I suspect that bigger speedups could come from karatsuba/cook/strassen-like tricks, coordinate system tricks, or other tricks.

Proof-of-stake users in this configuration emit signatures under a high-value key on a regular basis. Note that Ethereum 2 operates in the min-sig configuration.
